top_stories.title: Bitcoin ETFs See Nearly $1B Single-Day Inflow, Largest Since October 2025
points: Spot Bitcoin ETFs (investment funds that hold actual Bitcoin rather than futures contracts, letting investors gain exposure via regular brokerage accounts) took in nearly $1 billion in net inflows in a single day.
This is the strongest daily inflow performance since October 2025, following a prior week that saw just $6.2 million in inflows—the weakest week across 141 weeks of ETF trading history.
The surge coincided with Bitcoin's price rallying to $86,245, pushing the average ETF holder back into profit for the first time since January.
The rally is tied to broader macro tailwinds: falling oil prices, the Nasdaq hitting record highs, and continued accommodative Federal Reserve monetary policy.
The inflow surge signals renewed institutional confidence in Bitcoin's price trajectory and the regulatory environment for spot-based crypto investment products.

unique_angles.point: Bitcoin has cleared three key technical levels ($80K, $82.5K, $85K) in a three-session rally, with traders now assigning 79% probability to hitting $87.5K and pricing an $87.5K–$90K peak as the most likely September outcome (33% probability), while tail-end bets on $95K (12%) and $100K (4%) are cooling, suggesting the short squeeze (forced buying by traders who bet against rising prices) may be fading.

Thursday's Trump-Xi summit and the September 30 PCE inflation data release (landing on the same day as prediction market resolution) are seen as key catalysts that will determine whether the rally continues.

items.title: White-Hat Hackers Route Stolen Coldcard Wallet Bitcoin to Recovery Trust
points: Bitcoin stolen via a Coldcard hardware wallet exploit is being routed into a 'recovery trust' by white-hat hackers (ethical hackers who use their skills to help rather than harm).
This suggests a partial recovery effort is underway to return funds to victims of one of the larger recent crypto security breaches affecting hardware wallet users.

sections.title: Bitcoin ETF Momentum Surge
points: Nearly $1 billion in net inflows arrived Monday, compared to just $6.2 million the entire prior week—the weakest weekly inflow across 141 weeks of ETF trading history.
BTC price spike pushed average ETF holders back to profit for the first time since January, removing selling pressure from underwater positions.

Bitcoin is being lifted by the same macroeconomic factors boosting broader stocks: falling oil prices, Nasdaq at record levels, and a Federal Reserve still maintaining accommodative monetary policy despite recent rate increases.

sections.title: September Bitcoin Price Prediction Market
points: Bitcoin has already cleared $80K, $82.5K, and $85K support/resistance levels in a three-session rally.
Traders assign 79% probability to BTC reaching $87.5K (up from 74% on Monday), making an $87.5K–$90K peak the modal outcome at 33% probability.
Tail-end probabilities are cooling: $95K probability fell to 12% and $100K to just 4%, suggesting the short squeeze (forced buying to cover bets against rising prices) may be losing steam.
Thursday's Trump-Xi summit and September 30's PCE inflation print (landing on resolution day) will likely decide whether the rally continues.

sections.title: Coldcard Hardware Wallet Recovery Effort
points: Some Bitcoin stolen in the Coldcard hardware wallet exploit is being routed toward a 'recovery trust,' indicating white-hat hackers are attempting to recover and return funds to affected users.
This represents a partial recovery mechanism for one of the larger recent cryptocurrency security breaches affecting hardware wallet users.
